entry.title: Stop It, Brat
entry.summary: The sun was high. The weather was lovely. That part was for me. None of the rest of it was. Here is what happened, in the order the ship experienced it. Capitan Ostrand came out on deck with his cup, as he did every morning, and admired the weather, as he did every morning, and drank his tea with a noise like a bucket going down a well. The gulls were up. The water was that flat blue a sailor will tell you he likes and does not like. Then he saw something. No. He saw someone. And that someone was— "WOOOOOOOO." I...

entry.title: A Fish Too Big?
entry.summary: I was in the sea, and every breath I did not take was a decision I was taking, and the surface was a bright thing very far above me that I appeared to be arguing with instead of swimming toward. The sea knows I lied to it. That was the thought, when thought came. Not the rope. Not the fishermen. Just: there was a night on this water when I told it a prince had drowned, and the water has a long memory and no sense of humour, and it had been waiting for me to fall back into it. entry.title: An Oath of Blood
entry.summary: I, or maybe only my head, struck the stone floor and rolled, and came to rest at last against the foot of the old stone. The last thing I saw was my own body, headless, convulsing — and the fountain of it going up and out and over, endless, and the stone black with it, and the whole dome turning the colour of the inside of a mouth. Ah. So that is what kind of red it is. Then the light went out of my eyes, and the last thing I understood was that I had been wrong about the rose, and that being wrong about the rose...

entry.title: Altar of Gods
entry.summary: "Phew." My breath came back at me off the rock, loud, and I clamped my mouth shut on it. My right hand was closed around a crack in the cliff face about as wide as a bad promise, and the rest of me was hanging off it. I looked down. That was a mistake. The sea was doing something patient down there, the way it does when it has all night. I looked up instead. entry.title: Prologue
entry.summary: Snap — branches, leaves, something behind me shearing loose. I did not look. Looking cost time, and time was the only thing I had left. "There is no use running, Your Highness." An arrow went past my right ear close enough that I felt the air of it and nothing else. I gasped. My heart was a drum in a closed room, and the whole room was my skull.
